user.title: Add New City
user.description:
It appears that you have already configured QWeather. You may choose to **‘Use a new account’** or directly **‘Reuse the existing account’** information.
**Note:** Adding multiple cities under the same **API Host** will multiply the request volume. Please extend the update interval appropriately to avoid exceeding limits.

setup.title: Configure QWeather Pro
setup.description:
### Setup Steps
**Go to the [QWeather Console]({qweather_console}):**
1. In Settings, copy the **API Host** and fill it into the **API Host** field below.
2. Project Management → Create a project, then add credentials to the project: optional **JSON Web Token** and **API KEY**.
3. The location can be latitude and longitude (WGS-84) or a city name.
4. The default location is the HA latitude and longitude.
#### Note: API KEY authentication does not provide sufficient security. API KEY authentication will be subject to request limits. JSON Web Token (JWT) is recommended!

data.location_id: Geographical location. Only supports latitude and longitude (longitude first).
data.api_key: Ordinary API Key (Leave blank if using JWT)

jwt_setup.title: Configure JWT Security Authentication
jwt_setup.description:
A public key has been automatically generated for you.
**Steps:**
1. Copy the **public key** in the box below.
2. Go to the [QWeather Console]({qweather_console}), add a credential to your project, select **JSON Web Token**, and paste the public key.
```text
{public_key}
```
After completing this, fill in the **Project ID** and **Key ID** below.
#### Note: JWT authentication can only be added once. If you re-add the integration, the original JWT credential will no longer be valid.

reauth_confirm.description:
Your QWeather credentials are no longer valid. Please update your **API Host** and credential below. Your location settings will be preserved.
**Go to the [QWeather Console]({qweather_console})** to check your project and credentials.

reauth_jwt.description:
Please fill in the new **Project ID** and **Key ID** for JWT authentication. Your location settings will be preserved.
**Go to the [QWeather Console]({qweather_console})** to check your project and credentials.

init.title: Integration Options
init.description:
### Instructions for Use
- The daily forecast can be set to **3/7/10** days (V1 API supports up to 10 days).
- The hourly forecast can be set to **24/72/168** hours.

get_weather.name: Get weather data
get_weather.description: Return the full weather dataset for a QWeather Pro weather entity, including current conditions, daily/hourly forecasts, air quality, warnings, life indices and the smart weather abstract. Optionally restrict the response to specific top-level data blocks using 'keys'.

keys.name: Keys
keys.description: Optional list of top-level data blocks to return. Omit to return the entire dataset.

api_key_quota.title: QWeather API KEY daily quota
api_key_quota.description:
Your QWeather Pro integration is still using API KEY authentication.
Note: API KEY authentication does not provide sufficient security. Starting 2027-01-01, QWeather will limit daily requests for API KEY authentication (exact amount TBD), and SDK 5+ will drop API KEY support; JWT is unlimited and recommended. If you keep API KEY, polling defaults to 100 minutes; switch to JWT in "Reconfigure" for unlimited, faster updates.
